newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares climb on LUKoil but rise seen short. [CORRECTED 10:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian shares climb on LUKoil but rise seen short. [CORRECTED 10:52 GMT]

text.p: Shares of Russian oil company LUKoil rose on profit expectations, leading liquid shares higher at the open on Thursday, though traders said the market lacked funds flow for a rally of the most-traded shares.

Sberbank savings bank, hotly sought after after its listing on the Russian Trading System and showing tight share availability, rose to $185.00 at 0935 GMT on the Russian Trading System from $168.00 at the close on Wednesday.
The RTS index at 0800 GMT had ticked up to 359.98 from its closing 359.76.
"There is no reason for the blue chips to grow -- there is no money for them," Creditanstalt senior trader Andrei Galperin said, predicting leading shares could end up down for the day.
LUKoil, which forecast net profit by Russian cash accounting standards would grow to 4.0-4.5 trillion roubles in 1997 from 3.8 trillion in 1996, outperforming some analysts expectations.
LUKoil Holding shares, the most active on the market, rose to $15.42 from $15.30, but were off an early $15.55.
Aton trader Alexandra Petrova said investors were reallocating funds and that second tier shares where bargains are perceived to be waiting were seeing strong interest.
"People are looking for new opportunities," she said (corrects the name and the sex of the trader).
